metadata.name: Ecodesign for Zig
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Zig code: explicit allocator ownership, bounded buffers, tested failure paths.

memoire.name: Zig — allocators and buffers
memoire.description: Ownership is explicit in Zig; the cost is paying attention to it (RGESN Algorithms).

rules.title: Allocation without a matching defer
rules.description: Zig hands you the allocation and the responsibility. An alloc with no defer free leaks on every early return, and early returns are the normal control flow of a language built on error unions.
rules.recommendation: Pair every alloc with a defer free on the next line, and test the failure path with a failing allocator.

example.good:
const buf = try allocator.alloc(u8, n);
defer allocator.free(buf);

rules.note: One matching defer free, or an arena allocator, anywhere in the file silences the rule. An arena freed as a whole is a valid strategy, which is why it is excluded.

rules.title: Unbounded read from external input
rules.description: readAllAlloc with a large maximum lets whoever is on the other end decide how much memory you allocate. On a service that is a denial of service written as a convenience.
rules.recommendation: Set a maximum sized to what the format actually requires, or read into a fixed buffer in a loop.
